title: STAFFING SERVICES AGREEMENT
parties: Copperfield Staffing LLC / Demo Customer LLC
summary: Confidentiality trap, short renewal notice, no liability cap

pages.heading: Parties and effective date
pages.body: This Staffing Services Agreement is entered into by Copperfield Staffing LLC, a Texas limited liability company with its principal office in Austin ('Supplier'), and Demo Customer LLC, a Delaware limited liability company ('Customer'). The parties intend this Agreement to govern temporary and contract staffing supplied to Customer locations. This Agreement becomes effective on April 1, 2026 ('Effective Date'). Each party represents that the signatory is authorized to bind its organization. Capitalized terms used but not defined herein have the meanings given in later sections.

pages.heading: Initial term and renewal
pages.body: The initial term of this Agreement is twelve (12) months beginning on the Effective Date. Unless either party delivers written notice of non-renewal at least ten (10) days before the end of the then-current term, this Agreement will automatically renew for successive twelve (12) month periods on the same terms, except for fees adjusted under Section 3. Either party may propose updated commercial terms during the final sixty (60) days of a term. Failure to agree on revised fees before renewal does not prevent automatic renewal at the prior term's rates unless non-renewal notice is timely given.

pages.heading: Fees, invoicing, and total value
pages.body: Customer will pay Supplier for staffing services at the rates in Exhibit A. Supplier will invoice monthly in arrears for hours worked and approved expenses. Customer shall pay undisputed amounts within thirty (30) days of invoice date. The total contract value for the initial term is USD 96,000, inclusive of standard markups but excluding pass-through taxes and approved overtime unless Exhibit A states otherwise. Late payments may incur a finance charge of one percent (1%) per month on overdue balances, not to exceed the maximum permitted by law.

pages.heading: Termination for convenience
pages.body: Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon fifteen (15) days' prior written notice to Supplier, without need to cite cause, subject to payment for services rendered through the effective termination date and any non-cancellable third-party costs reasonably incurred in reliance on this Agreement. Supplier may terminate for convenience only if Customer fails to pay undisputed invoices after notice and cure. Upon termination, Supplier will cooperate to transition assigned personnel and return Customer property. Sections intended to survive will remain in effect.

pages.heading: Scope of staffing services
pages.body: Supplier will recruit, employ or engage, and assign qualified personnel to perform work under Customer's direction at designated sites. Assignments may include administrative, light industrial, or professional roles as described in work orders. Customer will provide safe working conditions, necessary training on Customer systems, and timely approvals of timesheets. Supplier remains responsible for payroll, statutory withholdings, and baseline background checks described in Exhibit B. Changes in scope require a written change order signed by both parties.

pages.heading: Service levels and performance
pages.body: Supplier will use commercially reasonable efforts to fill approved requisitions within ten (10) business days for standard roles and twenty (20) business days for specialized roles. Customer will rate fill time and quality monthly. Persistent failure to meet agreed fill targets for ninety (90) days constitutes a material performance issue curable under the default provisions. Service credits, if any, are listed in Exhibit C and are Customer's sole remedy for fill-time delays, excluding fraud or willful misconduct. Neither party guarantees uninterrupted staffing during force majeure events.

pages.heading: Acceptance of personnel
pages.body: Customer may reject a assigned worker within the first five (5) business days if the worker lacks required skills or fails background standards, and Supplier will provide a replacement at no additional search fee. After acceptance, Customer directs day-to-day work and may request replacement for performance reasons with reasonable notice. Supplier will not retaliate against workers for lawful Customer feedback. Acceptance of timesheets constitutes acceptance of hours worked except for documented disputes raised within ten (10) days of invoice.

pages.heading: Confidentiality
pages.body: Each party may receive non-public information from the other. The receiving party will protect such information using at least the same degree of care it uses for its own confidential materials, and no less than reasonable care. Confidential information may be used only to perform under this Agreement and may not be disclosed except to employees and advisors with a need to know who are bound by similar obligations. This strong confidentiality duty survives five (5) years after termination, except trade secrets, which remain protected as long as they qualify as trade secrets under applicable law.

pages.heading: Limitation of damages
pages.body: Except for breaches of confidentiality, indemnification obligations, or payment defaults, neither party will be liable to the other for any indirect, incidental, special, or consequential damages, including lost profits, lost revenue, or loss of goodwill, even if advised of the possibility of such damages. The foregoing limitation applies regardless of the form of action, whether in contract, tort, or otherwise. Each party acknowledges that direct damages remain recoverable subject to other provisions of this Agreement.

pages.heading: Governing law and disputes
pages.body: This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Texas, excluding conflict-of-law rules that would apply another jurisdiction's substantive law. The parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of state and federal courts located in Travis County, Texas for disputes arising under this Agreement. Either party may seek injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to protect intellectual property or confidential information. Prevailing party may recover reasonable attorneys' fees only if a court awards them under Texas law.

pages.heading: Insurance
pages.body: Supplier will maintain workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability insurance with limits of at least USD 500,000, and commercial general liability of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence. Upon request, Supplier will furnish certificates of insurance naming Demo Customer LLC as certificate holder. Customer will maintain its usual property and general liability coverage for its premises. Failure to maintain required insurance is a material breach if not cured within thirty (30) days of notice.

pages.heading: Assignment and subcontracting
pages.body: Neither party may assign this Agreement without the other party's prior written consent, except that either party may assign to an affiliate or in connection with a merger or sale of substantially all assets with notice. Supplier may subcontract payroll or background screening if subcontractors are bound by obligations no less protective than this Agreement. Any prohibited assignment is void. Subject to the foregoing, this Agreement binds and benefits the parties and their permitted successors.

pages.heading: Notices
pages.body: Notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by email with confirmation, nationally recognized courier, or certified mail to the addresses in the signature block or as updated by notice. Notices are deemed given on receipt if delivered by courier, on the third business day if mailed, or when sent if email, unless a bounce-back indicates failure. Operational communications about schedules and timesheets may occur through Customer's vendor portal without satisfying formal notice requirements.

pages.heading: Intellectual property and work product
pages.body: Customer retains all rights in its pre-existing materials, trademarks, and business processes. Work product created solely by Supplier personnel in performing services, excluding Customer confidential information, is assigned to Customer upon full payment. Supplier retains general recruiting methods, templates, and know-how. Personnel inventions unrelated to Customer assignments remain with the inventor. Each party will execute reasonable documents to effectuate ownership as stated in this section.

pages.heading: Entire agreement and amendments
pages.body: This Agreement, including exhibits referenced herein, is the entire agreement between the parties regarding staffing services and supersedes prior proposals and oral understandings. Amendments must be in writing signed by authorized representatives of both parties. Waivers must be written and signed. If any provision is held invalid, the remainder continues in effect. Headings are for convenience only. Exhibits A through C are incorporated by reference when attached.
